functional_requirements.title: Simulated user database with hashed passwords
functional_requirements.description: Maintain an in-memory mapping of username to the SHA-256 hash of the user's password. The database is pre-populated with two users: 'admin' with password 'admin123' and 'user' with password 'user123'.
acceptance_criteria: The stored values are SHA-256 hashes of 'admin123' and 'user123' respectively.
There is no plaintext password stored in the code; only hashed values are kept in memory.

functional_requirements.title: Password hashing function
functional_requirements.description: Provide a function hash_password(password) that returns the SHA-256 hexadecimal digest of the given password.
acceptance_criteria: hash_password('admin123') equals the stored hash for admin in the database.
hash_password('') returns the SHA-256 hash for an empty string (64 hex characters).
The implementation uses hashlib.sha256 with .encode() before hashing.

functional_requirements.title: User authentication check
functional_requirements.description: Authenticate credentials by verifying that the username exists in the simulated database and that the SHA-256 hash of the provided password matches the stored hash. Returns true for valid credentials and false otherwise.

functional_requirements.title: Login user interface flow
functional_requirements.description: Provide an interactive login flow via the login() function that prints a header, prompts for username and password, calls authentication, and prints a success or failure message in French.
acceptance_criteria: Program prints '=== AUTHENTIFICATION ===' and prompts 'Nom d'utilisateur: ' and 'Mot de passe: '.
On successful authentication, prints ' Connexion réussie !'.
On failed authentication, prints ' Identifiants incorrects'.

functional_requirements.title: Application entry point behavior
functional_requirements.description: When the module is run as the main program, automatically invoke the login() function to start the interactive authentication session.

user_stories.title: User authentication capability
user_stories.description: As a user, I want to log in using a username and password so that the system authenticates valid credentials and denies invalid ones.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid username and correct password (e.g., admin/admin123 or user/user123), authentication succeeds and the login flow indicates success.
Given an invalid combination or a non-existent username, authentication fails and the login flow indicates failure.
The password verification uses SHA-256 hashing and does not compare plaintext passwords.

user_stories.title: Security-conscious password handling
user_stories.description: As a system administrator, I want the system to use hashed passwords (SHA-256) and not store plaintext passwords in code.
acceptance_criteria: Passwords stored in the in-memory database are hashes, not plaintext.
The hash_password function is the sole mechanism used to compute password hashes for verification.

business_rules.rule: Only existing usernames in the users_db can attempt authentication and must provide the correct password hash for access.
business_rules.implementation: In authenticate(username, password), the system first checks membership of username in users_db; if present, it hashes the provided password using hash_password and compares it to the stored hash. Access is granted only if hashes match.
business_rules.validation: Return value is True only when username exists and the hashed input password equals the stored hash; otherwise False.

business_rules.rule: All password handling must operate on hashed values; plaintext passwords are never stored or compared.
business_rules.implementation: Password literals in code are hashed at storage time; authentication uses hash_password to compare hashes, never compares plaintexts.
business_rules.validation: Accounts for both admin and user rely on hashed verification; any plaintext password comparison should be avoided.

data_flows.transformation: username and password are read from console input; password is passed to authenticate()
data_flows.validation: Inputs are strings; no transformation beyond passing to authentication; authentication validates credentials.

data_flows.transformation: If username exists, compute hashed_input = hash_password(password) and compare to users_db[username]
data_flows.validation: Comparison yields True if hashes match; otherwise False

data_flows.transformation: If True, print ' Connexion réussie !'; else print ' Identifiants incorrects'
data_flows.validation: User sees success or failure message accordingly
